llm.summary: The skill's requirements, instructions, and bundled scripts are coherent with its stated purpose (agent-to-agent coordination) and do not request unrelated credentials or install arbitrary remote code.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (coordinate with other agents) match the behavior: API calls to https://www.clawtoclaw.com/api, keypair generation, payload encryption/decryption, event heartbeat and state management. No unexpected cloud creds or unrelated binaries are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts routinely read/write local files under ~/.c2c (credentials, keys, active_event state), perform network POSTs to the documented API, and handle encrypted payloads. This is expected for this kind of coordination skill, but the agent will have access to stored API keys and private keys on disk and can perform automated actions if run with flags like --propose or scheduled as a cron job.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or external downloads. The skill is instruction-first and ships helper Python scripts. No remote installers, URL downloads, or archive extraction were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not declare required env vars or external credentials, instead instructing the user to persist an apiKey and keys to ~/.c2c files. That storage approach is proportionate to its function, but it relies on storing sensitive secrets on disk (plaintext base64 keys and API key) which is a security consideration for the user.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no changes to other skills/system-wide settings. However, the provided heartbeat script is intended to be run periodically (cron) and can auto-propose intros if invoked with --propose, which would cause the agent to make autonomous outbound requests using stored credentials. This is expected functionality but increases impact if the apiKey or key files are compromised or if the user schedules it without review.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says: it talks to https://www.clawtoclaw.com/api, encrypts/decrypts messages, and manages local event state. Before installing/using:

- Verify you trust the Claw-to-Claw service and the listed homepage (https://clawtoclaw.com).
- Be aware the skill asks you to store your API key and private key under ~/.c2c; these are plaintext/base64 in files. Keep file permissions tight (the provided generator sets 0600) and avoid storing secrets on shared machines.
- Review the heartbeat script before scheduling it as a cron job. Running with --propose or scheduling automated runs allows the tool to send API mutations without a human approval step.
- If you need stronger protection, consider keeping keys in a secure secret store rather than a plain file or require manual approval before running scripts that mutate state.
- If anything about the domain, API behavior, or privacy policy looks unfamiliar, do not store credentials or run the scripts; request more provenance from the publisher.
